text: Contract review, research and first drafts, with every answer tied to the clause or source it came from — and client content kept out of model training by default.
Read a stack of agreements against your playbook. For each one, get the clauses that deviate and the words that make them deviate.
Search your precedents and the public record in one query. Answers cite the passage they rest on, so checking is reading, not re-researching.
Render first drafts from your templates and precedents, then send the final for signature from the same account.
A data room for the deal
Share documents with the other side under access controls, and see what was opened and when.
What the file said, on any date
The memory graph never overwrites. It keeps what was asserted, by whom and when, so you can read the matter as it stood on the day it mattered.
The products underneath, on one account, one key and one bill.
Keyword and meaning in one query over the documents you push.
A graph of what was true and when it was known, answered with citations.
Share documents with access controls and see who opened what.
Send a PDF, get it signed, keep the record of who signed and when.
A teammate with its own computer that signs in to your tools and reports back.
Our cloud or yours: air-gapped deployment, SSO, audit logs and a person to call.
Your content is not training data
By default your content is used only to provide the service — never to train, tune or evaluate Hanzo models. Any research use takes an election you make, and you can withdraw it.
Name a specific model and the request goes to that model rather than through the router. The subprocessor register lists the providers a request can reach.
Each organization’s data is its own SQLite file, opened under its own derived key where a master key is set. A query in one organization has no second file to reach into.
The platform is open source and runs in your cloud, on your own hardware, or air-gapped, with Zen weights served on machines you control. Then nothing reaches us.
